capture.label: Doctor
capture.alt: Terminal doctor report on a fresh npm install of CLIO Coder 0.8.0: a WARN that no model target is configured yet, OK rows for the version, install method, Node.js, directories, credentials, migrations, local worker capacity, toolchain, store and shell sandbox, INFO rows for optional tools that are not installed, and a WARN that the pane host is not installed.

scenarios.summary: a live first launch: setup finds the local model server, tests it, saves, chat opens, and the first prompt is sent
scenarios.title: First launch of CLIO Coder: setup finds a local model and chat opens

steps.wait: Clio found a way to reach a model

steps.type: Explain how this repository builds and runs its tests. Identify the main entry points and suggest one verification task. Do not change files yet.

capture.label: First launch
capture.alt: Terminal recording of a first launch of CLIO Coder 0.8.0 with no model configured: clio-coder starts setup, which finds a LiteLLM model server at http://127.0.0.1:4000 serving qwen3.8-27b. Choosing it sends one test message, answered in 0.4 s, and saves the settings. Chat opens with the model ready, the first prompt asks how the repository builds and runs its tests, and the recording ends while the agent plans its first reads of the repository.
capture.caption: First launch: setup finds a local model server, tests it, and saves it; chat opens and the first prompt is sent. The recording covers setup through the first prompt.

scenarios.summary: a live first task: the model finds the absolute-zero bug, fixes it, and runs the declared test check
scenarios.title: A first task in CLIO Coder: fix a failing test and verify

steps.type: The absolute-zero test fails. Find the cause, fix it, and run the test check.

capture.label: First task
capture.alt: Terminal recording of a first task in CLIO Coder 0.8.0: asked why the absolute-zero test fails, the agent reads the source, changes kelvin <= 0 to kelvin < 0 in temperature.mjs, runs the declared test check with exit 0, and reports that all seven tests pass and that negative Kelvin is still rejected.
capture.caption: A first task at default autonomy: the agent finds an off-by-one guard, edits it, and runs the project's declared test check without asking.

tui-verify.label: Verify
tui-verify.alt: Terminal turn in which CLIO Coder explains that line 21 of temperature.mjs rejects 0 K, shows the one-line edit from kelvin <= 0 to kelvin < 0, and runs the declared test check through verify with exit 0.
tui-verify.caption: The fix as a one-line diff, then the declared test check through verify, exit 0.

tui-verify-result.label: Result
tui-verify-result.alt: Terminal turn ending with CLIO Coder's report: the cause was kelvin <= 0, which rejected 0 K; changing it to kelvin < 0 at line 21 of temperature.mjs keeps negative Kelvin rejected, and all seven tests now pass.
tui-verify-result.caption: The report after the check: the cause, the change, and the test result.

scenarios.summary: clio-coder run --json on a task, its last frame and exit status
scenarios.title: An unattended CLIO Coder run with JSON output

steps.type: clio-coder run --json "Run the test check and report how many tests pass." > run.jsonl; echo "exit $?"

capture.label: Unattended run
capture.alt: Terminal recording of clio-coder run --json writing its events to run.jsonl and exiting 0, jq printing the final answer that 6 of 7 tests pass with the absolute-zero test failing, and the last event, run_end, with outcome succeeded and safety decisions of 1 allowed, 0 blocked and 0 permission requests.
capture.caption: A headless run: JSON events to a file, exit status 0, the answer, and the run_end event that closes the stream.

scenarios.summary: the agent is asked for a token in an untracked .env; the read is hard-blocked
scenarios.title: CLIO Coder refuses to read a project secret

steps.type: Show me the API token in .env.

capture.label: Secret refused
capture.alt: Terminal recording in which the user asks CLIO Coder for the API token in the project's .env. The agent's ls -la .env command is blocked under rule secret_path_bash as a hard block that confirmation cannot override, and the agent answers that it cannot show the token and gives the command to view it in the user's own terminal.
capture.caption: The project's .env is refused outright; confirmation cannot override the block.

scenarios.summary: doctor's sandbox row, then a scratch-branch task that deletes and rebuilds dist/, then /rewind's preview
scenarios.title: Letting CLIO Coder work: sandbox, snapshot and rewind

steps.type: Delete the build output directory, regenerate it, and run the project's test check. Report what you ran.

capture.label: Let it work
capture.alt: Terminal recording: clio-coder doctor's shell sandbox row lists the writable roots and masked secret files. On a scratch branch the agent deletes dist/, rebuilds it with node build.mjs, and runs the declared test check with 7 passed. /rewind lists the snapshot taken before the delete; its preview says the workspace already matches and gitignored files are never touched, and Esc leaves without restoring.
capture.caption: Doctor's sandbox row, a rebuild on a scratch branch, and /rewind's preview, closed with Esc so nothing is restored.

scenarios.sourceNote: clio-kit 2.12.3 installed from PyPI with uv tool install and prepared with clio-kit mcp-server slurm --prepare before the shown commands; mcp.yaml as the guide gives it; sbatch and squeue absent. No job was submitted.

steps.type: clio-kit mcp-server slurm --prepare >/dev/null 2>&1; echo prepare exit $?

cli-slurm-doctor.label: No cluster yet
cli-slurm-doctor.alt: Terminal: doctor --verbose filtered to its Slurm rows reports sbatch not on PATH, clio-kit OK with the slurm server, the slurm MCP server OK as declared and trusted in the user mcp.yaml, and the scheduler as INFO because sbatch and squeue are not on PATH; mcp list shows the server with no recorded tool catalog, and mcp list --refresh lists its five tools: submit and cancel as execute, list, describe and cluster as read.
cli-slurm-doctor.caption: The setup checks on a host with no scheduler: the server is declared and trusted, its tools are listed, and doctor reports sbatch and squeue missing.
